newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer calls on EU nations to balance budgets.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer calls on EU nations to balance budgets.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Tuesday it was very important for nations seeking to join European monetary union to balance budgets in the medium-term or even achieve surpluses.

Tietmeyer said in a panel discussion at the Global 24 conference that budget consolidation measures would not harm economic growth and job creation but instead help create confidence to spur further investment.

"I would like to draw attention to the medium-term objectives, which are to bring deficits to zero or even to a surplus. That is the guiding principle for fiscal policy in Europe," Tietmeyer, speaking in English, told the conference.
"I think it is very important to bring it close to a very balanced consolidation of fiscal policy. It would not harm growth," he said.

"It is not really harming employment. It is creating the necessary confidence, if it is done in a convincing way. It is creating confidence for investors, and that is the basis where investment can really take place."
Tietmeyer said balanced budgets would avoid conflicts between monetary and fiscal policies and that current public budget levels were not yet sustainable.
"If that is really done, then we will avoid conflicts between monetary policy and fiscal policy," he said.

Tietmeyer said the institutional framework for a credible European monetary union was in place but reaffirmed that one-off measures to whip finances into shape to meet EMU entry criteria in the Maastricht Treaty would not be enough.
"One-off measures are not enough," Tietmeyer said. "They have to be supported by decisions which have a lasting effect."
Tietmeyer called on European countries, including Europe, to create more structural flexibility in their economies.
"We have to improve the structural situation in our countries. That means, of course, creating better conditions for employment," he said.

"I think it is very important for the lasting result of monetary union that we make more progress on the question of sound fiscal policy, bringing it to a sustainable situation and increasing the flexibility and reducing the rigidity in our markets," Tietmeyer said.
"I hope that the governments are making progress. I hope that the unions are making progress. It is very important that this progress become very visible in the next year," he said.
